text:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired (P3) — rule: inference.router.latency_99 > 1200ms — route: /v1/generate (us-east)
Sam: acked. I'm looking at the router dashboards now.
Priya: yep saw the blip on canary too, hitting 99th for ~30s. no user tickets yet. :thinking_face:
Sam: checking traces — canary/healthcheck spiked at the same time. going to tail logs.
Jules: throwing the canary query up: `avg:inference.canary.latency{env:prod}.rollup(60)` shows a 3-min pulse, last point back to baseline.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: incident PD-7890 acknowledged by Sam.
Sam: quick log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z router[svc-3]: route=/v1/generate lat=1350ms kv_hit=false shard=pool-a
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z canary[check-7]: exec=ok lat=1400ms retries=1
```
Sam: looks like a short-lived resource contention on pool-a; no scale events in logs.
incidentbot: Auto-resolve triggered (alert cleared by monitoring) — resolved after 65s.
Priya: auto-resolve. i'm keeping a small monitor on dashboards for 10m.
Sam: noted. leaving a note on PD.
(00:07 after initial) pd-bot: PagerDuty alert re-fired (same rule) — PD-7891 created, escalating per policy.
Lee: pinged for rotation. taking over.
Sam: handing off to @Lee — saw it look like canary jitter, no customer reports. I have traces if you need. :thumbsup:
Lee: thanks. can you paste the trace id?
Sam: trace: `trace-0a9f` — spans show a KV lookup spike + queueing on shard pool-a.
Jules: quick check on infra — pool-a GPU mem had a short OOM reclaim around the same time but no pod restarts. could be transient GC.
Priya: there was a cron retry from the analytics job at 14:01 that collided with canary traffic — not user traffic.
Lee: ok. i'll suppress the alert route for 10m and keep an eye. applying suppression now.
OpsBot: Alert suppression applied: scope=inference.router.latency_99 route=/v1/generate duration=10m by=Lee
Lee: reduced canary weight and temporarily muted synthetic checks while we watch.
Sam: good plan. any customer mentions?
Priya: checked support slack and Sentry — zero customer errors tied to that timeframe.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: PD-7891 acknowledged by Lee.
Lee: monitoring — dashboards look steady after suppression. latency back to baseline.
Jules: posting metric snapshot:
```
canary.latency (14:00-14:10):  p50=90ms p95=210ms p99=320ms (spike at 14:02 to 1400ms)
router.errors: 0 -> no visible 5xxs
kvmem.pool-a: slight bump then normal
```
Lee: verdict: noisy synthetic canary + cron overlap caused ephemeral flapping. no customer impact.
Sam: filing follow-up ticket to tune the canary and add a short-term suppression rule for repeat-fires within 2m.
Priya: assign to eng-runtime to adjust canary schedule and add jitter on retry jobs.
Lee: created INFR-2145 (tune canary + suppression logic). linking this thread.
Jules: follow-up action: change alert condition to require 2 consecutive 60s buckets before firing (reduce single-bucket noise).
Lee: agreed. i'll own the hotfix. handing back to Sam as next on rotation in 30m.
Sam: thanks — i'll check back before I go. :eyes:
pd-bot: PagerDuty: PD-7890 and PD-7891 resolved (auto-clear + manual suppression).
incidentbot: thread closed — no customer impact, follow-up ticket INFR-2145 created.
Sam: closing with :white_check_mark: — nice quick handoff, thanks everyone.
